vritti_extracts.madhaviya_dhatuvritti: radha himsayama. svadishu parasmaipadi sakarmaka anit. snau pratyaye radhnoti iti rupam sidhyati. asya himsa-arthe prayogah prasiddhah.
vritti_extracts.kshiratarangini: radha himsayama. svadau snuh. radhnoti, radhnuta, radhnuvanti. himsa pida vadho va iti kshirasvami.

meanings.English: to hurt, to injure, to torment, to destroy
meanings.Bengali: aaghat kara, himsa kara, jantrana deoya

dhaturupanandini.simple_explanation: The root 'sādh' belongs to the 5th (Svādi) class and means 'to accomplish, succeed, or bring to fruition'. In the present tense, it receives the Svādi-vikaraṇa 'nu', producing 'sādhnoti' (he/she accomplishes). In the causative form with the affix 'ṇic', it becomes 'sādhayati' (he/she executes, establishes, or proves something).

scenarios.grammar_trigger: svādi-gaṇa laṭ-lakāra (kartari parasmaipada)
scenarios.example_english: Through diligent effort, people accomplish all their tasks.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: ṇic-pratyaya (causative) laṭ-lakāra
scenarios.meaning: causes to succeed, executes, or establishes/proves
scenarios.example_english: The logician proves his proposition with rational arguments.

vritti_extracts.madhaviya_dhatuvritti: The root sādhī~ is read in the Svādigana in the sense of saṃsiddhi (complete accomplishment, perfection). Being marked with an ītvam / anudāttet, it attaches the śnu vikaraṇa in sārvadhātuka environments, yielding sādhnoti, sādhnutaḥ, sādhnuvanti. In liṭ-lakāra, abhyāsa-kārya and guṇa yield sasādha, sedhatuḥ, sedhuḥ.
vritti_extracts.kshiratarangini: Kshirasvamin defines sādhī~ saṃsiddhau as denoting the culmination and attainment of a desired goal. It conjugates via the 5th gaṇa affix 'snu/nu', distinguishing it from similar 1st or 4th gaṇa roots, and is used transitively for fulfilling tasks or intransitively for succeeding.

meanings.English: to accomplish, achieve, complete, succeed, or prove
meanings.Hindi: siddha karnā, pūrā karnā, saphal honā
meanings.Bengali: siddha karā, sampanna karā, saphal haoyā

dhaturupanandini.simple_explanation: The verbal root 'skambh' belongs to the fifth conjugation (svadigaṇa) and means to support, prop up, arrest, or obstruct. In the present tense, it takes the class sign 'snu' (which undergoes specific Vedic and classical alternations such as skabhnati or skabhnoti) and is conjugated in Parasmaipada. In causative constructions (nic), it conveys causing something to be propped up or firmly supported.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: Kartari prayoga, Lat lakara, Prathama purusha, Ekavacana
scenarios.example_english: The pillar supports the roof/structure.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: Nic pratyaya (Causative), Lat lakara, Prathama purusha, Ekavacana
scenarios.meaning: causes to prop up or fastens firmly
scenarios.example_english: The builder props up the wall using wood.

vritti_extracts.madhaviya_dhatuvritti: The root 'skambhu' is listed in the svadi-gana with the sense 'pratibandhe' (holding back, propping, or restraining). The final 'u' is an it-marker indicating that it belongs to the stambhadi class of roots which allow specific suffixal replacements (such as śnā or śnu) and loss of nasals in specific derivations under the sutra 'stambhustumbhuskambhuskumbhumāñca'.
vritti_extracts.kshiratarangini: Kshirasvamin explains 'skambhu pratibandhe' as stambhana-hetutve (serving as a support, restraint, or arresting mechanism). Along with roots like stambh, stumbh, and skumbh, it forms part of the sautra and svadi clusters exhibiting Vedic-classical alternate stems.

meanings.English: to prop, support, arrest, obstruct

dhaturupanandini.simple_explanation: The root aś (aśūṅ) belongs to the 5th class (Svādigaṇa) and means to pervade, spread throughout, or attain/reach. Because of the indicatory marker 'ṅ' (ṅit), it strictly takes Ātmanepada endings in standard active usage, taking the class sign 'nu' (śnu) to form 'aśnute' (he/she pervades or attains).

scenarios.grammar_trigger: svādi class kartari prayoga (active voice), ātmanepada, prathama puruṣa, ekavacana
scenarios.example_english: The light pervades the entire universe.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: liṭ lakāra (perfect tense), prathama puruṣa, ekavacana
scenarios.example_english: The scholar reached fame everywhere.

vritti_extracts.madhaviya_dhatuvritti: The root 'aśūṅ' is taught in the sense of 'vyāpti' (pervasion, reaching). The nasal 'ṅ' designates it as anudātteṅit, yielding Ātmanepada affixes. It takes the 'snu' class-affix (svādibhyaḥ snuḥ) in sārvadhātuka environments, yielding forms such as aśnute, aśnuvāte, aśnuvate, and in lit, ānaśe.
vritti_extracts.kshiratarangini: Kshirasvamin explains 'vyāpti' as encompassing or reaching completely ('vyāpya sthitiḥ'). The derivation follows the standard svādi rules with anit characteristic in non-periphrastic secondary formations.

meanings.English: to pervade, to reach, to attain

dhaturupanandini.simple_explanation: The root 'yu' belongs to the 5th group (Svadi gana) and uniquely carries two opposite meanings: to blend/mix together and to separate/unmix. It inserts the infix '-nu-' before adding endings. Parasmaipada (yunoti) is used when the mixing or separating is done externally, whereas Atmanepada (yunute) is used when the action reflects back upon the agent.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: lat-lakara (present tense), prathama-purusha (3rd person), ekavacana, parasmaipada
scenarios.example_english: The wise person mixes water with milk.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: lat-lakara (present tense), prathama-purusha (3rd person), ekavacana, atmanepada
scenarios.meaning: He/she separates or blends for oneself
scenarios.example_english: The sage separates virtues and faults for himself.

vritti_extracts.madhaviya_dhatuvritti: The root 'yu' belongs to the Svadi class and takes the 'snu' vikarana affix, expressing both connection (misrana) and disconnection (amisrana/vislesha). Being ubhayapadi, it conjugates as yunoti and yunute. The vowel undergoes guna to 'o' before sarvadhatuka affixes lacking an it-marker.
vritti_extracts.kshiratarangini: Kshirasvamin notes that 'yu' operates with dual semantic polarity: it signifies both samsarga (unification/mixture) and vivikta/prithak-karana (separation). Forms are generated with snu affix yielding yunoti and yunute.

meanings.English: to mix, join, unite, separate, unbind

dhaturupanandini.simple_explanation: The root 'vṛ' (vṛñ) belongs to the 5th group (Svadi gana) and means 'to choose', 'to select', or 'to serve/honor'. It is an Ubhayapada verb, which means it can take both Parasmaipada and Atmanepada endings. In general usage, Parasmaipada denotes selecting or honoring in an active sense, whereas Atmanepada expresses choosing or selecting for oneself (like choosing a partner or path). Adding the causative affix transforms it into 'varayati/varayate', meaning 'to cause to choose' or 'to invite/woo'.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: Svadi class affix 'snu' + Parasmaipada present tense 3rd person singular
scenarios.example_english: The noble person chooses the path of truth.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: Svadi class affix 'snu' + Atmanepada present tense 3rd person singular
scenarios.example_english: The maiden chooses a suitable groom for herself.

vritti_extracts.madhaviya_dhatuvritti: The Madhaviya Dhatuvritti notes that 'vṛñ sambhaktau' carries the sense of sambhakti (selection, respectful honoring, and serving). Taking the Vikarana affix 'snu' by 'svadibhyah snuh', it undergoes Guna of the root to 'ar' before strong affixes, yielding 'vṛṇoti' and 'vṛṇute'. Because of the anubandha 'ñ', it is conjugated in both Padas.
vritti_extracts.kshiratarangini: Kshirasvamin in Kshiratarangini explains 'vṛñ sambhaktau' as indicating intentional selection, sharing, or adoration. It is distinguished from the Kryadi root 'vṛñ' primarily through Vikarana assignment (snu vs sna) and retains Anit status in principal conjugational forms.

meanings.English: to choose, to select, to serve, to honor
meanings.Bengali: boron kora, bachhai kora, sheba kora

dhaturupanandini.simple_explanation: The root 'tṛṇ' belongs to the 5th group (Svadi gana) and means 'to eat' or 'to graze/consume'. It takes the infix 'nu' in the present tense to form 'tṛṇoti' in active voice (Parasmaipada). When used in causative (Nic), it means 'to feed' or 'to cause to eat'.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: kartari prayoga (active voice, lat-lakara, 3rd person singular)
scenarios.example_english: The deer eats grass in the forest.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: nic-pratyaya (causative, lat-lakara, 3rd person singular)
scenarios.example_english: The cowherd feeds grass to the cow.

vritti_extracts.madhaviya_dhatuvritti: tṛṇu adane svādirudāttaḥ parasmaibhāṣaḥ. nuvikaraṇaḥ. tṛṇoti tṛṇutaḥ tṛṇvanti. adanārthe prayujyate.
vritti_extracts.kshiratarangini: tṛṇu adane. tṛṇoti. bhakṣaṇārthe svādigaṇe pathitaḥ.

meanings.English: to eat, to graze, to consume

dhaturupanandini.simple_explanation: The root 'tud' means to prick, push, or inflict pain. In the Tudadi class, it takes the marker 'śa' (which does not cause vowel strengthening), keeping the root vowel short as 'u' (tudati/tudate). It can be conjugated in both Parasmaipada and Atmanepada without a change in basic meaning.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: Kartari prayoga (Parasmaipada, Lat-lakara, Prathama-purusha, Ekavacana)
scenarios.example_english: The boy pricks the leaf with a needle.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: Causative (Nic-pratyaya, Lat-lakara, Prathama-purusha, Ekavacana)
scenarios.example_english: The wicked person causes distress to good people with harsh words.

vritti_extracts.madhaviya_dhatuvritti: The root 'tuda vyathane' is the opening entry of the sixth class. Under the rule 'tudādibhyaḥ śaḥ', the vikarana 'śa' is added. Because 'śa' is treated as having an indicatory 'ṅ' (ṅidvadbhāva via srvadhātukam apit), guna of the laghūpadha vowel is blocked, yielding forms like 'tudati' and 'tudate'. It is classified as aniṭ.
vritti_extracts.kshiratarangini: Kshirasvamin notes 'tuda vyathane' implies tormenting, striking, or inflicting affliction. He highlights the absence of sarvadhatuka guna due to the 'śa' affix and confirms its dual-pada (ubhayapada) nature and anit status in ardhadhatuka environments.

meanings.English: To pain, to prick, to vex, to strike

dhaturupanandini.simple_explanation: The root 'nud' means to push, drive, impel, or dispel. Being an Ubhayapadi verb in the Tudadi class (6th Gana), it takes both Parasmaipada and Atmanepada endings with the infix 'sa' (causing no guna change to the short vowel 'u'). In the active voice, both forms mean pushing or driving away something.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: Kartari prayoga (Parasmaipada, Lat lakara, prathama-purusha, eka-vacana)
scenarios.example_english: The sun dispels the darkness.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: Kartari prayoga (Atmanepada, Lat lakara, prathama-purusha, eka-vacana)
scenarios.example_english: The wind drives away the cloud.

vritti_extracts.madhaviya_dhatuvritti: nuda prerane. tudadi-gane ubhayapadi anit. natva-nishedhadir na bhavati dhatvadau natvasya satvat.
vritti_extracts.kshiratarangini: nuda prerane. nodayati nudati nudate. preranam preritam kshepanam ca.

meanings.English: to push, drive, impel, remove, dispel

dhaturupanandini.simple_explanation: The root diś primarily means to give, bestow, point out, or assign. As a member of the Tudadi gana, it takes the class marker 'śa' (which leaves 'a') without causing guna strengthening to the penultimate short vowel 'i', yielding the base diśa-. It can take both Parasmaipada and Atmanepada endings. Prefixing prepositions (upasargas) modifies the meaning significantly: 'upa' creates upadiśati (teaches, instructs), and 'ā' creates ādiśati (commands, orders).

scenarios.grammar_trigger: Present tense (lat), Kartari prayoga (Active voice), Parasmaipada, 3rd person singular
scenarios.example_english: The guide points out the path.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: Lat lakara with upasarga 'upa', 3rd person singular
scenarios.example_english: The teacher imparts knowledge to the student.

vritti_extracts.madhaviya_dhatuvritti: diśa atisarjane. atisarjanaṃ nāma dānam utsarjanaṃ vā. śaḥ pratyayaḥ, laghūpadhaguṇābhāvaḥ. svaritittvād ubhayapadī. anit.
vritti_extracts.kshiratarangini: diśa atisarjane. atisarjanam dānam, anye tu preṣaṇam iti vyācakṣate. anudāttopadeśatvāt anit, ubhayatobhāṣaḥ.

meanings.English: to point out, show, assign, grant, bestow

dhaturupanandini.simple_explanation: The root 'lip' means to smear, anoint, or plaster a surface. Being in the Tudadi class and belonging to the muc-adi subgroup, it inserts a nasal sound 'm' before the consonant 'p' in the present tense, forming 'limp-'. It is Ubhayapada, meaning it can take active endings (limpati) or middle endings (limpate) without changing the core meaning.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: Parasmaipada (Active voice)
scenarios.example_english: The attendant anoints the body with sandalwood paste.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: Causative (Nic-pratyaya)
scenarios.example_english: The homeowner gets the wall plastered.

vritti_extracts.madhaviya_dhatuvritti: The root 'lipa upadehe' belongs to the Tudadi gana and is Ubhayapadi. By the sutra 'śe mucādīnām', it receives the augment 'num' (nasal infix) in sarvadhatuka affixes before the marker 'śa', yielding 'limpati' and 'limpate'. It is classified as anit.
vritti_extracts.kshiratarangini: Kshirasvamin notes 'lipa upadehe' signifies coating, smearing, or spreading a substance over an object. The augment 'num' gives the base 'limp-', and in non-conjugational tenses without 'num', the root forms 'lepsyati' and 'lipta'.

meanings.English: to smear, anoint, coat, plaster, spread upon

dhaturupanandini.simple_explanation: The root 'kṣip' belongs to the 6th class (Tudadi) and means 'to throw', 'to hurl', or 'to send'. Because it belongs to the Tudadi class, it takes the thematic conjugational marker 'śa' (which appears as 'a' without guna strengthening of the penultimate vowel, keeping the 'i' as short 'i'). It can be conjugated in both Parasmaipada (when the action is general) and Atmanepada (often when the result of the action reflects on the agent). Adding the causative affix 'ṇic' gives the meaning 'to cause someone to throw or dispatch'.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: Kartari prayoga, Parasmaipada, Lat lakara (present tense, 3rd person singular)
scenarios.example_english: The boy throws the ball.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: Kartari prayoga, Atmanepada, Lat lakara (present tense, 3rd person singular)
scenarios.meaning: He/She casts or directs towards oneself/inwardly.
scenarios.example_english: The warrior releases an arrow for his own purpose.

vritti_extracts.madhaviya_dhatuvritti: The root 'kṣipa preraṇe' is anudāttet and svara-bhedena ubhayabhāṣā. Because it is in Tudadi-gana, the vikaraṇa 'śa' prevents guṇa by 'kṅiti ca', retaining the radical 'i' as short: kṣipati, kṣipate. In lit-lakāra, it forms cikṣepa, cikṣipatuḥ, cikṣipuḥ in Parasmaipada, and cikṣipe in Atmanepada. It is anit in standard ardhadhatuka environments (kṣeptā, kṣepsyati).
vritti_extracts.kshiratarangini: Kshirasvamin notes 'kṣipa preraṇe' as denoting throwing, casting, or propelling. It forms kṣipati and kṣipate taking the thematic marker 'śa'. The past passive participle is formed with anit rules as 'kṣipta'.

meanings.English: to throw, cast, hurl, send, direct

dhaturupanandini.simple_explanation: The root 'mris' primarily means to touch, feel gently, or to mentally examine and reflect upon something. Belonging to the Tudadi group (6th conjugation), it takes the intermediate affix 'sa', which prevents the vowel 'ri' from changing to 'ar' in normal present tense forms (giving 'mrisati'). With prefixes like 'vi', it commonly means to deliberate or analyze carefully.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: Lat lakara (present indicative active, 3rd person singular)
scenarios.example_english: The sage contemplates the ultimate truth through meditation.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: Upasarga 'vi' + Lat lakara (present tense)
scenarios.example_english: The wise person thoroughly deliberates on the task.

vritti_extracts.madhaviya_dhatuvritti: mrisa amarsane. amarsanam sparsanam vivecanam ca. anit parasmaipadi. sa-pratyaye guna-pratisedhan mrisati iti rupam sidhyati.
vritti_extracts.kshiratarangini: mrisa amarsane. sparsane dhyane viveke ca vartate. sa-vikaranatvad guna-abhava misati.

meanings.English: to touch, stroke, deliberate, consider, examine
meanings.Hindi: sparsa karana, chuna, vicara karana, parakhna

dhaturupanandini.simple_explanation: The root krs in the 6th class (Tudadi) means to furrow, scratch, plough, or draw lines across a surface. In the Tudadi group, the root vowel does not undergo Guna strengthening before the Vikarana -sa-, resulting in the direct present form krsati. In causative (Nic) forms, it conveys causing someone to plough, cultivate, or furrow the ground.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: Kartari Prayoga (Active Voice, Tudadi Lat Lakara, Prathama Purusha Ekavacana)
scenarios.example_english: The farmer ploughs the field with a plough.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: Nic Pratyaya (Causative, Lat Lakara, Prathama Purusha Ekavacana)
scenarios.meaning: Causes to plough or causes to be tilled
scenarios.example_english: The landowner has the field tilled by the farm workers.

vritti_extracts.madhaviya_dhatuvritti: The Madhaviya Dhatuvritti clarifies that krs-a vilekhane in the Tudadi class takes the Vikarana -sa- (tudadyah sah) without Guna of the penultimate vowel, yielding krsati, krsatah, krsanti. It emphasizes the primary semantic sense of 'vilekhana' as creating incisions or tilling lines in the earth, distinguishing its base formation from the Bhvadi form karsati.
vritti_extracts.kshiratarangini: Kshirasvamin in Kshiratarangini glosses vilekhana as 'bhumyadeh vidarana-purvakam lekhana-karanam' (ploughing or tearing up the soil to make furrows). It notes the anit nature of the root in unaugmented finite environments and details alternations in non-Sarvadhatuka tenses.

meanings.English: to plough, to furrow, to till, to make furrows/scratches
meanings.Hindi: jotna, hal chalana, zamin khodna ya rekha khinchna
meanings.Bengali: chash kora, jomi chasano, anchod kata
meanings.Chinese: geng di, geng zuo, hua he

dhaturupanandini.simple_explanation: The root krs belongs to the Tudadi group and means to plough, scratch, or draw lines across the earth. Because it receives the specific class-affix 'sa' without vocalic strengthening (guna), its base remains 'krs-', yielding krsati (Parasmaipada) and krsate (Atmanepada). Adding the causative affix (nic) produces karsayati ('causes to plough').

scenarios.grammar_trigger: Kartari prayoga, Tudadi class affix 'sa' (Parasmaipada)
scenarios.example_english: The farmer ploughs the field.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: Hetumanni-nic (Causative active)
scenarios.example_english: The landowner causes the field to be ploughed by the farmers.

vritti_extracts.madhaviya_dhatuvritti: krsa vilekhane. vilekhanam nama bhumer vidaranam ksetrasamskaro va. tudaditvat sah, 'pugantalaghupadhasya ca' iti gunastveka-sesabhavat pratisedhah. krsati, krsate iti ubhayapaditvam.
vritti_extracts.kshiratarangini: krsa vilekhane. vilekhanam dharanyadeh ksetrikaranam. sarvadhatuke sa-pratyaye gunabhavat krsati krsate iti sidhyati.

meanings.English: to plough, to furrow, to scratch, to cultivate
meanings.Bengali: chash kora, hal dhora, achor kata

dhaturupanandini.simple_explanation: The root krt means to cut, split, or slice. Belonging to the Tudadi class and the special muc-adi subgroup, it inserts an internal nasal sound (n) before the final consonant in the simple present tense, transforming krt into krntati. When using the causative form (kartayati), it means causing someone or something to cut.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: kartari prayoga, lat lakara, prathama purusha, ekavacana (with muc-adi num-agama)
scenarios.example_english: The gardener cuts the branch.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: nic pratyaya (causative), kartari prayoga, lat lakara
scenarios.meaning: causes to cut / makes someone cut
scenarios.example_english: The master makes the servant cut the grass.

vritti_extracts.madhaviya_dhatuvritti: krti chedane. krtiti dirghaikaranto hyayam. she mucadinam iti num. krntati. cartisyati, kartisyati. cikarta. akartit, akratsit.
vritti_extracts.kshiratarangini: krti chedane. mucaditvan num krntati. anitkarikasvasya kartsyatikartisyatyorvetvamuktam.

meanings.English: to cut, to divide, to slice, to sever

dhaturupanandini.simple_explanation: The root 'muc' means to free, release, or let go. In the Tudadi group, it gains an internal nasal 'n' before standard endings, producing 'muñcati' in active voice and 'muñcate' in middle voice. Adding the causative suffix transforms it into 'mocayati', meaning to cause someone or something to be set free.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: Kartari Prayoga (Present Active, Parasmaipada, Tudadi-gana with num-infix)
scenarios.example_english: The archer releases the arrow.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: Causative (Nic-pratyaya, Kartari Prayoga)
scenarios.example_english: The king frees the prisoner from jail.

vritti_extracts.madhaviya_dhatuvritti: The root 'mucḷ' is classified under 'mocana' (the act of releasing or liberating). By the rule 'she mucādīnām', it receives a nasal num-agama before the sha-vikarana, resulting in the bases 'muñcati' and 'muñcate'. It is anit and ubhayapadi.
vritti_extracts.kshiratarangini: Kshirasvamin defines 'mucḷ mocane' indicating mokshana (letting loose, emitting, forgiving, or liberation). It carries the marker lri which governs anit status and undergoes regular guna in non-sarvadhatuka environments like 'moksyati'.

meanings.English: to release, to free, to let go, to discharge

dhaturupanandini.simple_explanation: The root 'pish' belongs to the sixth group of verbs (Tudadi-gana) and means to form, shape, adorn, or carve into components. When conjugated in the simple present tense (Lat lakara), it takes the marker 'sha' and gains an internal nasal sound 'm' (num-agama), resulting in the base form 'pimsha-'. In the causative (Nich), it changes to 'peshayati', expressing that someone causes another person to shape or decorate something.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: Kartari prayoga (active voice), Lat lakara (present tense), Prathama-purusha (third person), Ekavacana (singular)
scenarios.example_english: The sculptor shapes and carves the wood.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: Causative (Nich-pratyaya), Kartari prayoga, Lat lakara, Prathama-purusha, Ekavacana
scenarios.example_english: The teacher causes the student to carve the statue.

vritti_extracts.madhaviya_dhatuvritti: piSa avayave - avayavanam karanam rupakaranam ityarthah. she krtichidikhidipishibhyo num ityanena numagame krte pimshati iti rupam sidhyati. anidayam dhatuH.
vritti_extracts.kshiratarangini: piSa avayave - avayavo nirmanam rupashobha va. sha-pratyaye pare she krtichidi ityadina numagame pimshati iti bhavati.

meanings.English: to shape, to form, to adorn, to carve
meanings.Bengali: gathan kara, sajjita kara, rup deoya

dhaturupanandini.simple_explanation: The root 'ruś' means 'to harm', 'to hurt', or 'to injure'. Because it belongs to the 6th class (Tudādi Gaṇa), it adds the conjugational infix '-śa-' (which leaves '-a-'). Since this infix behaves as 'ṅit' (having a silent ṅ), it prevents the vowel 'u' from strengthening into 'o' in present-tense forms like 'ruśati'. In causative (ṇic), it causes someone else to harm or hurt, becoming 'rocayati'.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: kartari prayoga (active voice), laṭ-lakāra (present tense), prathama-puruṣa (3rd person), ekavacana (singular)
scenarios.example_english: The hunter injures the deer in the forest.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: ṇijanta (causative), kartari prayoga, laṭ-lakāra, prathama-puruṣa, ekavacana
scenarios.meaning: causes to injure / causes harm to
scenarios.example_english: The wicked person causes another to injure his enemy.

vritti_extracts.madhaviya_dhatuvritti: The root 'ruśa hiṁsāyām' is enumerated among the Tudādi class. Being anudāttet, it takes the 'śa' pratyaya in Sārvadhātuka affixes. By virtue of being marked with śit, the infix acts like a ṅit affix, preventing guṇa of the upadhā vowel 'u', yielding 'ruśati'. In Ārdhadhātuka affixes, guṇa applies normally, yielding forms such as 'rurośa', 'rokṣyati', and 'roṣṭā'.
vritti_extracts.kshiratarangini: Kṣīrasvāmin notes 'ruśa hiṁsāyām' immediately following 'riśa hiṁsāyām', glossing both as expressing destructive violence or infliction of bodily harm. It follows the standard aniṭ conjugation patterns of the sixth gaṇa without irregular vocalic lengthening.

meanings.English: to hurt, to injure, to harm
meanings.Hindi: chōṭ pahum̐cānā, hiṁsā karnā, dukh dēnā
meanings.Bengali: āghāt karā, hiṁsā karā, kṣati karā

dhaturupanandini.simple_explanation: The root 'kṛt' belongs to the Tudadi class and means 'to cut' or 'to sever'. In the present tense, by a special grammar rule for the mucādi subgroup, it inserts a nasal sound 'n' in the middle of the root, forming 'kṛntati' (he/she cuts). When made into a causative with the 'ṇic' suffix, it changes to 'kartayati' meaning 'causes to cut' or 'has something cut'.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: kartari prayoga (active voice), lat-lakara (present tense), prathama-purusha, eka-vacana
scenarios.example_english: The gardener cuts the branch of the creeper.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: nic-pratyaya (causative), lat-lakara (present tense), kartari prayoga
scenarios.meaning: causes to cut / makes someone cut
scenarios.example_english: The master has the grass cut by the worker.

vritti_extracts.madhaviya_dhatuvritti: The root 'kṛtī cchedane' is read with an īkāra it-marker. Beloging to the Tudadi group and specifically within the 'mucādi' sub-group, it undergoes num-āgama before the standard 'śa' vikarana per the sutra 'śe mucādīnām' (7.1.59), yielding the base form 'kṛnta-' and resulting in the present-tense form 'kṛntati'. In the perfect tense (lit), reduplication gives 'cakarta', 'cakṛtatuḥ', 'cakṛtuḥ'.
vritti_extracts.kshiratarangini: Kshirasvamin defines 'kṛtī cchedane' as the action of cutting or partitioning. He explains that due to its membership in the 'mucādi' gana, it takes the middle nasal insertion in the sarvadhatuka lakaras, generating forms like 'kṛntati', 'akṛntat', 'kṛntatu', and 'kṛntet'.

meanings.English: to cut, to sever, to divide, to slice

canonical_dhatvartha: roṣe (in the sense of anger, displeasure, or wrath)

dhaturupanandini.simple_explanation: The root 'ghud' belongs to the 6th group of verbs (Tudadi class) and means to become angry or display displeasure. In standard active voice (Parasmaipada), the subject experiences or expresses anger. When a causative affix (Nic) is added, it means to make someone else angry or provoke wrath.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: Simple present tense (Lat lakara), active voice (Parasmaipada)
scenarios.example_english: The foolish person becomes angry upon hearing the statement.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: Causative present (Nic-pratyaya with Lat lakara)
scenarios.meaning: Enrages or provokes someone to anger
scenarios.example_english: The wicked person provokes his friend to anger.

vritti_extracts.madhaviya_dhatuvritti: The root 'ghuda' is listed in the Tudadi class with the meaning 'roṣa' (anger or resentment). As a member of Tudadigana, it takes the class marker 'śa' (a-pratyaya without initial vowel guna) in sarvadhatuka affixes, forming 'ghuḍati'.
vritti_extracts.kshiratarangini: Kshirasvamin defines 'ghuda roṣe' as expressing the state of resentment and irritation. It belongs to the d-anta group of Tudadi roots and forms its active stem as 'ghuḍati' without internal strengthening in the present tense.

meanings.English: to be angry, to be displeased, to exhibit wrath

dhaturupanandini.simple_explanation: The root 'duph' belongs to the Tudadi class (6th conjugation) and denotes the action of injuring, striking, or harming. In the standard present tense, it takes the class sign 'sa' and optionally undergoes nasal insertion (num-agama), yielding forms like 'dumphati' or 'duphati'. In causative (Nic) constructions, it expresses causing someone to strike or inflict injury, taking the form 'dophayati'.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: kartari prayoga, lat lakara, prathama purusha, ekavacana with optional num-agama
scenarios.example_english: The hunter strikes the deer in the forest.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: nic pratyaya, kartari prayoga, lat lakara, prathama purusha, ekavacana
scenarios.example_english: The master causes the servant to strike the enemy.

vritti_extracts.madhaviya_dhatuvritti: The Madhaviya Dhatuvritti classifies 'dupha' within the group of roots ending in labial stops (tupadayah) in the Tudadi-gana bearing the sense of injury ('himsayam'). It notes the application of optional num-agama before sarvadhatuka affixes, forming both 'dumphati' and 'duphati', and confirms its parasmaipada orientation.
vritti_extracts.kshiratarangini: Kshirasvamin in Kshiratarangini groups 'dupha' alongside tupa, tupha, supa, and dupa under 'himsarthah'. He underscores that because it belongs to the Tudadi group, guna does not apply to the root vowel in simple active conjugations under the 'sa' vikarna, except where optional vocalic or nasal modifications are prescribed.

meanings.English: to strike, hurt, injure, or kill
meanings.Bengali: aghat kara, himsa kara, bedana deoya

dhaturupanandini.simple_explanation: The root 'spRs' primarily means 'to touch' or 'to make physical contact'. In the 6th class (Tudadi), the vikaranapratyaya 'sa' prevents vowel strengthening (guna), so the root retains its 'R' vowel to form 'spRsati'. When used with the causative affix (nic), it changes to 'sparsayati', meaning 'causes to touch' or 'places in contact with'.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: lat lakara (present tense), prathama purusha, ekavacana (parasmaipada)
scenarios.example_english: The boy touches the soft flower with his hand.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: nic pratyaya (causative), lat lakara, prathama purusha, ekavacana
scenarios.meaning: causes to touch / brings into contact
scenarios.example_english: The mother makes the child's hand touch the holy water.

vritti_extracts.madhaviya_dhatuvritti: spRsa samsparse. tudadi-gane parasmayipadi anit ayam dhatuH. tudAdibhyah sa-pratyaye pare kniti ca iti nisedhat guno na bhavati, tena 'spRsati' iti rupam sidhyati. lun-lakare sici 'sprs-mrsa-kRsa-trpa-drpam' iti niyamena asparksit ityadi rupam vikalpena asprksat ityapi bhavati.
vritti_extracts.kshiratarangini: spRsa samsparse. spRsati, pasparsa, sparsi-ta/sparsta, spraksta, asprksat/asparsit. sparso vayu-gunah, sparsanam indriyam iti kshirasvami-pratipadanam.

meanings.English: to touch, to feel, to perceive by touch, to reach

dhaturupanandini.simple_explanation: The root 'vid' in the 6th class (Tudādi) means 'to find' or 'to obtain'. Unlike other classes where 'vid' means to know or to exist, here it receives an internal nasal sound 'n' (num-āgama) before the class suffix, turning into 'vinda-'. It can be conjugated in both active voices (Parasmaipada and Ātmanepada) without a major change in core meaning, while adding the causative affix 'ṇic' turns it into 'vedayati' (causes to obtain/bestows).

scenarios.grammar_trigger: Kartari prayoga, Parasmaipada, Lat-lakara, Prathama-purusha, Ekavacana
scenarios.example_english: The boy finds a gem on the road.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: Kartari prayoga, Ātmanepada, Lat-lakara, Prathama-purusha, Ekavacana
scenarios.example_english: A truthful person gains fame everywhere.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: Hetumati ṇic (Causative), Kartari prayoga, Parasmaipada, Lat-lakara, Prathama-purusha, Ekavacana
scenarios.meaning: causes to obtain / makes available / presents
scenarios.example_english: The teacher causes the student to attain knowledge.

vritti_extracts.madhaviya_dhatuvritti: The root 'vidḹ' is read in the Tudādi-gana in the sense of 'lābha' (attainment/acquisition). By the special rule 'śe mucādīnām', the augment 'num' is inserted before the class affix 'śa' in sārvadhātuka contexts, resulting in the base 'vinda-'. It forms 'vindati' and 'vindate' in the present tense, and 'vividatuḥ' / 'vividuḥ' in the perfect tense without the infix.
vritti_extracts.kshiratarangini: Kshirasvamin emphasizes that this root is distinct in sense and morphology from 'vid jñāne' (Adādi) and 'vid sattāyām' (Divādi). Having the 'ḹ' anubandha, it is marked as Ubhayapadī and anit, undergoing nasal insertion to yield 'vindati-vindate' in the non-perfect active paradigms.

meanings.English: to find, to obtain, to acquire, to gain

dhaturupanandini.simple_explanation: The root krs belongs to the 6th class (tudadi-gana) and means to plough, draw lines, or scratch. Unlike 1st-class roots, tudadi roots take the 'sa' vikarana which does not cause guna strengthening of the root vowel in basic present forms, giving 'krsati'. In the causative (nic), it takes guna/vriddhi yielding 'karsayati' (causes to plough or furrow).

scenarios.grammar_trigger: kartari prayoga, lat-lakara (present tense), prathama-purusha, eka-vacana
scenarios.example_english: The farmer ploughs the field.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: nic-pratyaya (causative), lat-lakara, prathama-purusha, eka-vacana
scenarios.meaning: causes someone to plough / makes someone furrow
scenarios.example_english: The landowner makes the farmer plough the soil.

vritti_extracts.madhaviya_dhatuvritti: krsa vilekhane - tudadi parasmaipadi anit. Tudatvat sa-vikarane na guna-pravrttih, tena krsati iti rupam sidhyati. Vilekhanam ksetradi-karshanam.
vritti_extracts.kshiratarangini: krsa vilekhane. Krsati. Vilekhanamiti bhumi-bhedanam ityarthah.

meanings.English: to plough, to furrow, to scratch, to cultivate

dhaturupanandini.simple_explanation: The root 'sprsh' belongs to the Tudadi class (6th conjugation) and primarily means 'to touch' or 'to make physical contact'. In the standard active voice (Kartari), the person directly touches an object using the thematic affix 'sha' (a), giving forms like 'sprishati'. When converted to causative (Nic), it means 'causes to touch' or 'sprinkles/contacts indirectly', taking the form 'sparshayati'.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: Kartari prayoga, Lat lakara, Prathama purusha, Ekavacana
scenarios.example_english: The boy touches the flower.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: Causative (Nic), Lat lakara, Prathama purusha, Ekavacana
scenarios.meaning: causes to touch / brings into contact
scenarios.example_english: The mother brings the baby in contact with water.

vritti_extracts.madhaviya_dhatuvritti: The Madhaviya notes 'spr̥śa saṃsparśane' as a tudadi-gana, anit root conjugated with the vikarana 'śa' without guna of the vowel r̥ in sarvadhatuka affixes, forming 'spr̥śati'. In lit, it takes double forms due to ralsyan-samprasarana rules, resulting in pasparśa. The anit status governs ardhadhatuka operations.
vritti_extracts.kshiratarangini: Kshirasvamin highlights that 'spr̥śá' indicates physical and perceptual contact (saṃsparśana). It is classified as anit and parasmaipadi, showing s-stem transformations in aorist (lun) such as aspārkṣīt or asprākṣīt via optional r-vowel positioning.

meanings.English: to touch, to contact, to perceive by touch

dhaturupanandini.simple_explanation: The root 'iS' belongs to the Tudadi group and means 'to desire', 'to wish', or 'to want'. In four common present-system tenses (Sarvadhatuka), the root undergoes a special letter replacement from 'iS' to 'icch' (forming 'icchati'). It is primarily used in the active voice (Parasmaipada) to express an individual's conscious wish or aim for something.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: Kartari prayoga (Present indicative / Lat lakara, 3rd person singular)
scenarios.example_english: The boy desires (wants) a fruit.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: Nic pratyaya (Causative active voice / Lat lakara, 3rd person singular)
scenarios.example_english: The mother motivates (causes) the child to desire study.

vritti_extracts.madhaviya_dhatuvritti: iSu icchayam. tudadih parasmaipadi anit. 'isho gamiyamikatinam cha' iti sutrena shapratyaye pare isha-dhatoh 'ccha' iti adesho bhavati, tena 'icchati' iti rupam siddhyati. lit-lakare 'iyesa', lut-lakare 'esita' va 'esta' ityadi rupani sambhavanti.
vritti_extracts.kshiratarangini: iSu icchayam. anit tudadih. sarvadhatuke vishaye 'iccha' iti adeshe krite icchati, aicchat, icchet, icchatu iti rupani bhavanti. ardhadhatuke tu guna-vriddhyadi karyani niyamena pravartante.

meanings.English: to desire, to wish, to want, to seek

dhaturupanandini.simple_explanation: The root 'kṛt' means to cut, split, or divide into parts. In the present tense, it belongs to the Tudadi class and takes a nasal insertion (num-agama), yielding the form 'kṛntati' in the basic active voice (Kartari Prayoga). When transformed into the causative (Nic), it signifies making someone cut or having something severed, taking the form 'kartayati'.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: Kartari Prayoga (Present Active, 3rd Person Singular)

vritti_extracts.madhaviya_dhatuvritti: The Madhaviya Dhatuvritti highlights 'kṛtī chedane' as an idit root in the Tudadi group that receives a medial nasal augment (num) in Sarvadhatuka environments via the special sutra 'kṛtīchedane...', leading to forms like kṛntati and kṛntataḥ. Being anit, it drops the intermediate i-kar in Ardhadhatuka forms such as kartā and kartum.
vritti_extracts.kshiratarangini: Kshirasvamin notes under 'kṛtī chedane' that the insertion of num is obligatory in non-causative personal endings, resulting in the stem kṛnta-. He contrasts it with its gunated Ardhadhatuka forms (kartana, kartita in causative) where the nasal augment is absent.

meanings.English: to cut, divide, sever, chop

dhaturupanandini.simple_explanation: The root 'kṝ' means to scatter, pour, or disperse. In the present tense (Tudādi gaṇa), the root vowel 'ṝ' changes to 'ir' with the affix 'śa' (a), giving 'kirati'. When prefixes like 'vi' or 'sam' are attached, the meaning shifts to intensely scattering all around or gathering and spreading.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: Kartari prayoga (active voice), Lat lakara (present tense), prathama-purusha eka-vacana

vritti_extracts.madhaviya_dhatuvritti: The root 'kṝ vikṣepe' belongs to Tudādi gaṇa and takes Parasmaipada endings. By the rule 'ṛta iddhatoḥ' (8.2.77), the radical long 'ṝ' undergoes substitution to 'ir' followed by ra-para, resulting in forms like 'kirati', 'kirataḥ', 'kiranti'. In lit-lakāra, it forms 'cakāra', 'ceratuḥ', 'ceruḥ'.
vritti_extracts.kshiratarangini: Kshirasvamin notes 'kṝ vikṣepe' as expressing scattering, spreading, and throwing forth. The radical vowel is replaced by 'ir' in särvadhātuka environments before the Tudādi vikarana 'śa'.

meanings.English: to scatter, strew, disperse, pour out

dhaturupanandini.simple_explanation: The root bhrasj means to roast, parch, or fry. In the present tense, its letters undergo a special change to form bhrjjati or bhrjjate. When the benefit of the cooking goes generally or to someone else, Parasmaipada (bhrjjati) is used. When one roasts or fries something for one's own consumption, Atmanepada (bhrjjate) is chosen. In the causative, it means causing someone to roast or fry.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: kartari prayoga, parasmaipada, prathama-purusha, eka-vacana
scenarios.example_english: The cook roasts barley grains in the pan.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: kartari prayoga, atmanepada, prathama-purusha, eka-vacana
scenarios.example_english: The ascetic roasts seeds for himself.

vritti_extracts.madhaviya_dhatuvritti: bhrasja pake - tudadi ubhayapadi anit root. In sarvadhatuka affixes, special euphonic changes (samprasarana and jash-tvadi) take place leading to the stem bhrjja- resulting in bhrjjati and bhrjjate. In lit and other ardhadhatuka forms, it optionally admits agama variants (bharjjayati, babhrajja, babhroja).
vritti_extracts.kshiratarangini: bhrasja pake - refers specifically to dry roasting or parching (bharjana-rupa-pake), distinct from water boiling (kvanatha or shrapana). Yields forms bhrjjati and bhrjjate in tudadi.

meanings.English: to roast, to fry, to parch, to bake

dhaturupanandini.simple_explanation: The root viś means 'to enter'. In its primary form without prefixes, it takes Parasmaipada endings with the Tudadi class marker 'śa', yielding 'viśati' (enters). When combined with the prefix 'ni-', Panini's rule 'neviśaḥ' triggers Atmanepada endings to mean 'settles down' or 'encamps'. Adding the causative affix (ṇic) changes the meaning to 'causes to enter' or 'admits'.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: Basic active voice (Kartari Prayoga) with Tudadi vikaraṇa 'śa'
scenarios.example_english: The boy enters the school.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: Preceded by prefix 'ni' triggering Atmanepada by Sutra 1.3.17 (neviśaḥ)
scenarios.example_english: The sage settles down in the forest.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: Causative affix (ṇic) with guṇa strengthening
scenarios.example_english: The attendant ushers the guest into the house.

vritti_extracts.madhaviya_dhatuvritti: viśa praveśane. tudādir aniṭ parasmaipadī. tudādibhyaḥ śaḥ iti śa-pratyayaḥ. śiti guṇapratiṣedhād viśatīti rūpam. lit-lakāre viveśa, viviśatuḥ, viviśuḥ. luṭi veṣṭā, lṛṭi vekṣyati. 'neviśaḥ' ity anena ni-pūrvāt ātmanepadaṁ bhavati, yathā niveśate senā.
vritti_extracts.kshiratarangini: viśa praveśane. aniṭ. śakārāntaḥ. viśati, viveśa. 'neviśaḥ' iti niviśate. praveśanaṁ nāma antar-gamanaṁ nīḍādisu sthirībhāvaś ca.

meanings.English: to enter, to penetrate, to settle, to go into

dhaturupanandini.simple_explanation: The root ksip belongs to the Tudadi class (Class 6) and fundamentally means to throw, fling, or direct. Because it takes the Tudadi marker 'sa' (a) without applying guna to the root vowel in simple present, it forms ksipati / ksipate. Being Ubhayapadi, it takes Parasmaipada when the action is generally directed outwards and Atmanepada when the result of the throwing or casting reflects back upon the agent. In the causative (Nic), the root vowel undergoes guna to become ksep- and takes the suffix -ayati (ksepayati), meaning 'causes to throw' or 'dispatches'.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: Kartari prayoga, Tudadi class-sign (sa), Parasmaipada, Lat lakara, prathama-purusa, eka-vacana
scenarios.example_english: The boy throws the ball.

scenarios.example_english: The king causes the soldier to shoot (throw) an arrow.

vritti_extracts.madhaviya_dhatuvritti: The Madhaviya Dhatuvritti categorizes ksipa prerane under the Tudadi class. It notes that the vowel does not take guna in Sarvadhatuka affixes due to kniti ca, yielding forms like ksipati and ksipate. It is anit in the ardhadhatuka forms (e.g., ciksepa, ciksipe, ksepta, ksetsyati), retaining its core sense of casting, flinging, and urging.
vritti_extracts.kshiratarangini: Kshirasvamin analyzes ksipa in the meaning of prerana (to impel, toss, or cast away). He emphasizes its status as an anit ubhayapadi root in the sixth gana, illustrating that derived nominals such as ksepa (delay or throwing) and niksepa (deposit or casting down) arise directly from the primal semantic shade of casting or urging.

meanings.English: to throw, cast, fling, send, direct

dhaturupanandini.simple_explanation: The root picc belongs to the 6th class (Tudadi) and means to divide, partition, or press. In the present tense, it receives a special nasal infix (num), transforming into 'piñcati' (divides). In causative (Nic), it changes to 'piñcayati' or 'piccayati' meaning 'causes someone to divide or crush'.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: Lat lakara, Prathama-purusha, Eka-vacana, Kartari prayoga

scenarios.grammar_trigger: Nic pratyaya (Causative), Lat lakara, Prathama-purusha, Eka-vacana
scenarios.example_english: The master makes the artisan divide the timber.

vritti_extracts.madhaviya_dhatuvritti: The Madhaviya Dhatuvritti details 'piccī vibhājane' as a Tudadi root taking the 'num' infix (augment) in Sarvadhatuka environments ending with 'śa', thereby deriving 'piñcati'. Its primary sphere of meaning is vibhajana (separation, division, or crushing into pieces).
vritti_extracts.kshiratarangini: Kshirasvamin glosses 'piccī vibhājane' by emphasizing the morphological transformation via 'num' augmentation producing the form 'piñcati', signifying the physical dividing or portioning of material objects.

meanings.English: to divide, partition, separate, crush

meanings.Chinese: fen ge, fen kai, po kai

dhaturupanandini.simple_explanation: The root sic means to sprinkle, pour, or water. In the present tense, it receives an extra nasal sound (num-agama) before the ending, changing to sincati (Parasmaipada) and sincate (Atmanepada). When used with causative affixes, it becomes secayati, meaning to make someone water or cause to sprinkle.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: Kartari prayoga, Parasmaipada, Lat-lakara, Prathama-purusha, Ekavacana
scenarios.meaning: He or she sprinkles or waters

vritti_extracts.madhaviya_dhatuvritti: The Madhaviya Dhatuvritti notes shica ksharane as an Ubhayapadi root of the Tudadi class. Under the influence of the muc-adi class rule, it receives num-agama yielding sincati and sincate in Sarvadhatuka environments. It is anit in primary formations and exhibits guna as sec- in Ardhadhatuka forms.
vritti_extracts.kshiratarangini: Kshirasvamin specifies shica as denoting ksharana (discharging, sprinkling, or dripping). Initial retroflex sha reverts to dental sa by Dhatvadeha sha-sha-sah. The insertion of num produces the intermediate stem sinc-, giving standard forms sincati and sincate.

meanings.English: to sprinkle, to water, to pour, to emit

dhaturupanandini.simple_explanation: The root 'kṛṣ' in the Tudadi class means to plough, scratch, or till the soil. Because it belongs to the sixth conjugation (Tudadi), the tense marker 'śa' prevents the middle vowel 'ṛ' from strengthening into 'ar', producing forms like 'kṛṣati'. In the causative form, it means to cause someone to plough or till.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: kartari prayoga (active voice, present tense, parasmaipada)

scenarios.grammar_trigger: ṇijanta (causative voice, present tense, parasmaipada)

vritti_extracts.madhaviya_dhatuvritti: The root 'kṛṣa vilekhane' is enumerated in the Tudadi-gana. Due to the sarvadhatuka affix 'śa', there is no guna of the root vowel 'ṛ', resulting in the form 'kṛṣati'. It is aniṭ in standard non-periphrastic forms and denotes furrowing, tearing open the earth, or tilling.
vritti_extracts.kshiratarangini: Kshirasvamin glosses 'vilekhanam' as 'bhūmeḥ vidāraṇam' (splitting or breaking up the soil). He highlights the contrast between the un-strengthened Tudadi forms ('kṛṣati') and the guna-strengthened Bhvadi forms ('karṣati').

meanings.English: to plough, to till, to furrow

dhaturupanandini.simple_explanation: The root 'tṛph' belongs to the 6th verb class (Tudādi Gaṇa) and primarily means to strike, injure, or kill. In standard active voice (Kartari Prayoga), it takes intermediate nasalization (num-āgama) in present tense conjugation to form 'tṛmphati'. When used in the causative (ṇijanta) form, it expresses causing someone to strike or harm.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: Kartari Prayoga (Present Tense, Parasmaipada, Lat Lakāra)
scenarios.example_english: The hunter strikes the deer in the forest.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: Causative Form (Nic-pratyaya, Kartari Prayoga)
scenarios.meaning: causes to strike or inflicts injury through someone
scenarios.example_english: The king causes his soldiers to harm the enemy.

vritti_extracts.madhaviya_dhatuvritti: The root 'tṛphi~ hiṃsāyām' receives the augment num by the rule 'idito num dhātoḥ' yielding nasalized forms such as 'tṛmphati' in the Sārvadhātuka present tense, signifying destruction or hurting.
vritti_extracts.kshiratarangini: Kshirasvamin notes 'tṛphi hiṃsāyām' among roots expressing injury; its penultimate vowel remains unchanged in Tudādi thematic conjugation while taking the medial nasal insert.

meanings.English: to injure, hurt, kill, or strike
meanings.Bengali: hingsā karā, āghāt karā, badh karā
meanings.French: blesser, faire du mal, frapper, tuer

dhaturupanandini.simple_explanation: The root 'kuc' belongs to the 6th class (Tudadi) and fundamentally means to contract, shrink, or curve inward. In basic active forms (Parasmaipada), it describes an entity curling up or shrinking naturally. When combined with the causative suffix (Nic) or preverbs like 'sam-', it shifts to actively causing something to contract, compress, or hesitate.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: Simple present tense (Lat), active voice (Kartari Prayoga), 3rd person singular
scenarios.example_english: The leaf curls up (shrinks) due to the cold.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: Causative form (Nic-pratyaya) with prefix 'sam-'
scenarios.example_english: The tortoise draws in (contracts) its limbs.

vritti_extracts.madhaviya_dhatuvritti: The Madhaviya Dhatuvritti glosses 'kuca samkocane' under Tudadi gana. It takes the Vikarana 'sha' without Guna of the stem vowel in Sarvadhatuka forms (yielding kucati). In perfect tense (Lit), it forms kukoce/kucoca with Set augment in Ardhadhatuka environments.
vritti_extracts.kshiratarangini: Kshirasvamin notes 'kuca samkocane' as indicating contraction or reduction of physical extent (samkoco hrasvibhavah). It is classified as Parasmaipadi and undergoes regular Tudadi thematic conjugation.

meanings.English: to shrink, to contract, to bend, to curl up

dhaturupanandini.simple_explanation: The root 'sic' means to sprinkle, pour, or water. In Tudadi gana, it takes the 'num' augment before the consonant ending and is inflected in both Parasmaipada (active focus on the action/object) and Atmanepada (middle focus). In the causative, it means causing someone to sprinkle or irrigate.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: Parasmaipada (Kartari prayoga, Lat lakara)
scenarios.example_english: The gardener waters the trees with water.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: Atmanepada (Kartari prayoga, Lat lakara)
scenarios.example_english: The farmer irrigates his own field.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: Nic pratyaya (Causative, Parasmaipada)
scenarios.meaning: causes to water / causes to sprinkle
scenarios.example_english: The master makes the servant water the plants.

vritti_extracts.madhaviya_dhatuvritti: ṣica kṣaraṇe tudādiḥ ubhayapadī anit. 'kṣaraṇaṃ' secanaṃ sravaṇaṃ vā. 'lipisicihvaśca' iti vartamānatvāt aṅ-ādeśavidhiḥ liṅ-ādau viśeṣaśca. num-āgame siñcati siñcate iti rūpe bhavataḥ.
vritti_extracts.kshiratarangini: ṣica kṣaraṇe. anit ubhayatobhāṣaḥ. kṣaraṇaṃ secanam. siñcati siñcate. asiñcat asikta. secako bhavati.

meanings.English: to sprinkle, to water, to pour, to emit

dhaturupanandini.simple_explanation: The verbal root 'mṛś' primarily means to touch, feel, examine, or ponder over something carefully. Belonging to the Tudadi group, it takes the thematic infix 'śa' (a) without taking guna strengthening in the present tense, yielding 'mṛśati'. When transformed into the causative (Nic), it conveys making someone reflect upon or examine a matter.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: Kartari prayoga (active voice), Lat lakara (present tense), prathama-purusha (third person), ekavacana (singular)
scenarios.example_english: The scholar deliberates upon the truth with his intellect.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: Causative (Nic-pratyaya), Kartari prayoga, Lat lakara, prathama-purusha, ekavacana
scenarios.meaning: causes to consider or reflect upon
scenarios.example_english: The teacher makes the student reflect on the deeper secret.

vritti_extracts.madhaviya_dhatuvritti: mṛśa āmarśane. āmarśanaṃ sparśanam parāmarśo vicāraṇaṃ cetyarthaḥ. tudāditvāt śaḥ, laghūpadhaguṇābhāvaḥ. mṛśati, mamarśa, mraṣṭā, mrakṣyati, amrākṣīt.
vritti_extracts.kshiratarangini: mṛśa āmarśane. sparśe parāmarśe vicāre ca vartate. śasi mṛśati. mraṣṭā mārkṣyati ityādi rūpāṇi bhavanti.

meanings.English: to touch, deliberate, examine, reflect upon

dhaturupanandini.simple_explanation: The root masj primarily means to dive, submerge, bathe, or purify oneself by plunging into water. In the present tense (Tudaadi class), the cluster sj changes to jj, yielding forms like majjati. When used with prefixes like ni- (nimajjati), it specifically conveys sinking or diving deep. In the causative (nic), it changes to majjayati, meaning to immerse or drown something.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: kartari prayoga, lat-lakaara, prathama-purusha, eka-vacana
scenarios.example_english: The fish dives happily in the water.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: nic-pratyaya (causative), lat-lakaara, prathama-purusha, eka-vacana
scenarios.example_english: The father immerses the vessel in water.

vritti_extracts.madhaviya_dhatuvritti: tumasjo shuddhau. anudaatto parasmaibhaashah. tu-ityasya tuphalaartham prayojanam. masjeranta aadesho jiti jityevaadi suutraih majja-bhaavah.
vritti_extracts.kshiratarangini: masjo shuddhau shuddhikarane nimajjane ca. tudanta-gana-pathitatvaat shapam baadhitvaa sha-pratyayah. majjati, mamajja, mankshyati.

meanings.English: to sink, to dive, to bathe, to submerge, to become pure
meanings.Hindi: dubna, gota lagana, snaan karna, shuddh hona
meanings.Bengali: nimojjito howa, dub dewa, snaan kora
meanings.French: plonger, s immerger, se baigner, se purifier

dhaturupanandini.simple_explanation: The root 'spṛś' means 'to touch'. In the Tudadi group, it takes the standard 'śa' affix, yielding the basic present-tense form 'spṛśati' (he or she touches). When combined with prefixes like 'upa-', it specifically denotes ceremonial sipping or touching of water for purification.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: Kartari prayoga (active voice), Lat lakara (present tense), 3rd person singular
scenarios.example_english: The boy touches the flower.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: Causative (Nic pratyaya), Lat lakara (present tense), 3rd person singular
scenarios.meaning: causes to touch / brings into contact
scenarios.example_english: The mother causes the baby to touch the tree.

vritti_extracts.madhaviya_dhatuvritti: spṛśa saṁsparśane. anit parasmaipadī. tudāditvāt śaḥ. spṛśati, pasparśa, spraṣṭā sparṣṭā vā, sprakṣyati sparkṣyati vā, asprākṣīt aspārkṣīt aspṛkṣat vā.
vritti_extracts.kshiratarangini: spṛśa saṁsparśane. śakārāntaḥ anit. spṛśati, pasparśa. ṛkārāt parasya ṣatve vikalpena rāgamāhuḥ.

meanings.English: to touch, to feel, to perceive by contact

dhaturupanandini.simple_explanation: The root 'dṛt' belongs to the sixth (Tudadi) class and means 'to respect, honor, or show high regard'. In the present tense, it takes the thematic vowel 'a' (vikarana 'sa') directly without initial guṇa strengthening in common forms, yielding 'dṛtati'. When used in causative (nic), it means 'to cause someone to respect or hold in esteem' (daratayati / dardarayati).

scenarios.grammar_trigger: Kartari prayoga (active voice), Lat lakara (present tense), prathama-purusha (third person), ekavacana (singular)
scenarios.example_english: The student constantly respects the teacher.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: Kartari prayoga (active voice), Lan lakara (past imperfect), prathama-purusha (third person), ekavacana (singular)
scenarios.example_english: The king honored the scholar in the assembly.

vritti_extracts.madhaviya_dhatuvritti: driti adare tudadih parasmaipadi. adarah sammananam pujanam ca. 'krticrtidrtitrkhi' ityadinam sa-pratyaya-vishaye gunabhavah vishistavidhi-sahitah pratipadyate. dhatoh prayoge sammananartho vyajyate.
vritti_extracts.kshiratarangini: drtir adare. tudadi-gana-pathitah. adarah priyabhavena bahumananam. dritati, adritat ityadi rupani sidhyanti.

meanings.English: to respect, to honor, to show regard, to care for
meanings.Hindi: adar karna, samman karna, aadar dena
meanings.Bengali: ador kora, somman kora, shraddha kora
meanings.French: respecter, honorer, estimer, avoir des egards

dhaturupanandini.simple_explanation: The root 'sphul' means to vibrate, quiver, dart, or fly off like a spark. In its normal form, it takes the 6th Gana infix 'sa' (a) without vowel strengthening, producing 'sphulati'. When used in causative (nic), it means to cause to shoot out or disperse, appearing as 'spholayati'.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: Kartari prayoga (active voice), Lat lakara (present tense), 3rd person singular
scenarios.example_english: A spark darts out from the fire like lightning.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: Nich-pratyaya (causative), Kartari prayoga, Lat lakara
scenarios.example_english: The person strikes the log and causes sparks to fly out.

vritti_extracts.madhaviya_dhatuvritti: The root 'sphula samcalane' belongs to Tudadi-gana and is categorized as Parasmaipadi and Anit. By application of the 'sa' vikaranapratyaya, the sarvadhatuka vowel does not undergo guna, yielding 'sphulati'. In the perfect tense (Lit), it forms 'pusphola', and with ardhadhatuka suffixes taking it-agama optionally or standardly, forms like 'spholita' and 'sphulita' are derived in accordance with morphological rules.
vritti_extracts.kshiratarangini: Kshirasvamin defines 'sphula' in the sense of 'calane' (motion, trembling, flashing). He notes its parallel behavior to roots like 'sphura', retaining the unstrengthened medial 'u' in tudadi present-stem conjugations.

meanings.English: to shake, flutter, quiver, dart, flash

dhaturupanandini.simple_explanation: The root 'spṛś' belongs to the 6th class (Tudadi) and means 'to touch' or 'to feel'. It takes the Tudadi-class infix 'śa' (a) without causing guna lengthening of the core vowel in the present tense, producing 'spṛśati'. In causative (Nic), it expresses 'causing to touch' or 'sprinkling/smearing' as 'sparśayati'.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: Simple Present (Lat Lakara, Parasmaipada, 3rd Person Singular)
scenarios.example_english: The child touches the flower.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: Causative Present (Nic Pratyaya, Lat Lakara, Parasmaipada)
scenarios.meaning: Causes someone to touch / brings into contact
scenarios.example_english: The mother causes the child to touch the water.

vritti_extracts.madhaviya_dhatuvritti: Madhaviya confirms 'spṛśa saṃsparśane' in Tudadi gana as an anit, parasmaipadi root. In sarvadhatuka forms like lat, guna does not occur due to the nit-vat status of the infix sa (spṛśati). In lit, reduplication forms 'pasparśa'. Multiple aorist (lun) formations like asprākṣīt / aspārkṣīt / aspṛkṣat occur per special Paninian rules for roots ending in s-sounds with r-vowels.
vritti_extracts.kshiratarangini: Kshirasvamin notes that 'spṛśa' strictly denotes physical contact or perceptual touch (saṃsparśana). It is an anit root taking parasmaipada affixes, yielding 'spṛśati' in the present and 'sparṣṭum' or 'spraṣṭum' in the infinitive.

meanings.English: to touch, to perceive by touch, to come into contact with

dhaturupanandini.simple_explanation: The root kṛś primarily means to make thin, to attenuate, or to become lean. In the basic Tudadi present tense (using the affix śa), it takes Parasmaipada endings without guṇa strengthening of the root vowel 'ṛ', yielding kṛśati. In causative constructions (nic), it adopts the meaning of actively causing someone or something to become thin or emaciated, forming karśayati.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: Kartari prayoga, Tudadi vikarana śa, Lat lakara, prathama-purusha eka-vacana
scenarios.example_english: The sage's body grows lean through penance.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: Causative (nic pratyaya), Lat lakara, prathama-purusha eka-vacana
scenarios.meaning: Causes to become emaciated / wears down
scenarios.example_english: Fasting diminishes strength.

vritti_extracts.madhaviya_dhatuvritti: krisha tanukarane tudadirudanit parasmaipadi. krishati. tanukaranam karsanamiti artha. asya anit-tvan nityam kridanta-rupani it-rahitani bhavanti yatha krishitavyam na bhavati kintu krashtavyam ityadi.
vritti_extracts.kshiratarangini: krisha tanukarane. krishati. krikara-rupatvat shasi gunabhavah. tanubhava-karana-kriyah. krishtah ityatra anittvam.

meanings.English: to make lean, to attenuate, to emaciate, to become thin
meanings.Hindi: dubala hona, kshina hona, patala karna
meanings.Chinese: bian shou, xiao shou, shi bian xi

dhaturupanandini.simple_explanation: The root 'srj' belongs to the 6th group of verbs (Tudadi-gana) and takes the base conjugation suffix '-a-' (sa). In its basic active voice (Parasmaipada), it conveys releasing, letting go, discharging, or bringing into existence (creating). When augmented with the causative suffix (Nic), it changes to 'sarjayati', meaning to cause to release, to cause to emit, or to dismiss.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: kartari prayoga (present active indicative, 3rd person singular, Tudadi class)
scenarios.example_english: Brahma creates the universe.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: nic-pratyaya (causative, present active indicative, 3rd person singular)
scenarios.meaning: causes to release / discharges / sends forth
scenarios.example_english: The king dispatches (causes to go/send forth) the messenger to the village.

vritti_extracts.madhaviya_dhatuvritti: The root 'srja visarjane' is listed under Tudadigana as anit and parasmaipadi. Visarjana denotes relinquishing, casting forth, producing, or creating (utsarga/nirmana). In lit-lakar, reduplication yields 'sasarja' and 'sasrjuh'. In lun, it forms 'asrakṣit' as anit root with vriddhi before s-suffix, and also optionally forms 'asrajat' by specific sutras.
vritti_extracts.kshiratarangini: Kshirasvamin notes 'srja visarjane utsarge' - functioning in the sense of letting go, discharging, or producing. The root follows the tudadi class marker 'sa' giving 'srjati' without guna in sarvadhatuka stems due to the git-nature of the suffix.

meanings.English: to create, to release, to emit, to let loose

dhaturupanandini.simple_explanation: The root 'tras' means to be frightened, agitated, or to tremble with fear. In its basic active form (Kartari Prayoga), it describes a person or animal experiencing fear. When converted into the causative form (trasayati), it shifts the meaning to actively scaring or frightening someone else.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: Lat lakara, Prathama-purusha, Eka-vacana (Simple Present Active)
scenarios.example_english: The deer is frightened of the tiger.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: Nich-pratyaya (Causative Active)
scenarios.example_english: The tiger scares all the deer.

vritti_extracts.madhaviya_dhatuvritti: trasI udvege: tudadi-gane parasmepadi set dhatuH. Udvego bhayam calanam canavasthitiH. Sa-pratyayena trasati iti rupam sidhyati.
vritti_extracts.kshiratarangini: trasI udvege: udvego bhayakampanadi-rupaH cittasya vikaraH. Tudadi-gana-pathena trasati trasataH trasanti ityadi.

meanings.English: to tremble, to fear, to be frightened or agitated

dhaturupanandini.simple_explanation: The root 'lis' belongs to the sixth group (Tudadi gana) and is conjugated in the Atmanepada. It primarily expresses diminishing, becoming small, shrinking, or moving lightly. When used in regular present tense, it takes the form 'lisate'. In causative constructions with the suffix 'nic', it changes to 'leshayati' or 'leshayate', shifting the meaning to 'causes to shrink' or 'lessens something'.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: Kartari prayoga (present tense active voice with Atmanepada inflection, Lat lakara)
scenarios.example_english: In autumn, the river diminishes.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: Nic pratyaya (causative, Parasmaipada, Lat lakara)
scenarios.example_english: The farmer reduces the portion of grain.

vritti_extracts.madhaviya_dhatuvritti: The Madhaviya Dhatuvritti analyzes 'lisa' in the Tudadi gana with the twin meanings of 'alpibhava' (lessening/shrinking) and 'gati' (movement). It is inherently Anit and takes the Tudadi-sa vikarana forming 'lisate' in the sarvadhatuka lakaras, exhibiting no guna of the root vowel in simple stems.
vritti_extracts.kshiratarangini: Kshirasvamin notes in Kshiratarangini that 'lisa' signifies contraction or diminution ('tanukaranam' / 'alpibhavah'). Being an Anit root of the Tudadi class with Atmanepada endings, the medial vowel 'i' remains unaltered in non-guna contexts.

meanings.English: to diminish, to become small, to shrink, to move
meanings.Bengali: chhota howa, kshino howa, kome jaowa
meanings.Chinese: bian xiao, jian shao, suo xiao

dhaturupanandini.simple_explanation: The root 'kṛt' belongs to the Tudadi class (6th conjugation) and means 'to cut' or 'to sever'. When conjugated in the present tense, it receives the special 'num' infix (a nasal 'n') before the final consonant, transforming the base into 'kṛnt-', producing forms like 'kṛntati'. In causative usage, it becomes 'kartayati' ('causes someone to cut').

scenarios.grammar_trigger: Kartari Prayoga (Present Tense, 3rd Person Singular, Lat)
scenarios.example_english: The woodcutter cuts the branch with an axe.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: Causative (Nic-pratyaya, Present Tense, Lat)
scenarios.meaning: causes to cut / has someone cut
scenarios.example_english: The farmer makes the worker cut the grass.

vritti_extracts.madhaviya_dhatuvritti: The Madhaviya Dhatuvritti explains 'kṛtī chedane' as an ikāranubandha root in the Tudadi group. It highlights that by the rule 'kṛtādibhyaḥ kartari śe num', the root admits the num-agama (nasal insert) when followed by the sarvadhatuka affix 'śa', resulting in the stem 'kṛnta-'. It also notes its veṭ nature in ardhadhatuka contexts under the 'kṛtyādibhyaḥ pañcabhyaḥ' provision.
vritti_extracts.kshiratarangini: Kshirasvamin in Kshiratarangini defines 'kṛtī' under 'chedane' (division, incision, cutting). He outlines the morphological modification where the intermediate num infix produces 'kṛntati' in the basic kartari present paradigm, contrasting it with simple thematic roots and noting the optional iṭ-augment application in general ardhadhatuka operations.

meanings.English: to cut, to sever, to divide

canonical_dhatvartha: kautilye alpībhāve ca (in the sense of crookedness, bending, and shrinking or diminution)

dhaturupanandini.simple_explanation: The root 'kruñc' means to bend, make crooked, curve, or shrink. In the basic active voice (Parasmaipada), it describes a subject naturally curling, shrinking, or bending. When converted into the Causative (Nic) form, it expresses making something bend, fold, or contract.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: Kartari Prayoga (Active Voice, Lat Lakara, Prathama Purusha, Ekavacana)
scenarios.example_sanskrit: bhaye sati sarpaḥ svasya vapuḥ kruñcati.
scenarios.example_english: Out of fear, the snake coils/contracts its body.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: Causative (Nic-pratyaya, Lat Lakara, Prathama Purusha, Ekavacana)
scenarios.meaning: Causes to bend or causes to shrink/fold
scenarios.example_english: The craftsman bends the wooden rod.

vritti_extracts.madhaviya_dhatuvritti: The Madhaviya Dhatuvritti notes kruñcu in the sense of 'kautilye alpībhāve ca' (crookedness and shrinking). It is classed under Tudadi gana with the vikaranapratyaya 'śa', producing kruñcati without medial guna. It functions both transitively and intransitively depending on the semantic context.
vritti_extracts.kshiratarangini: Kshirasvamin in Kshiratarangini explains that the root denotes 'saṃkoca' (contraction/shrinking) as well as 'vakrībhāva' (becoming curved or bent), sharing semantic and morphological affinities with other Tudadi guttural/palatal consonant roots.

meanings.English: to bend, to curve, to contract, to shrink, to make crooked
meanings.Chinese: wan qu, shou suo, suo xiao

dhaturupanandini.simple_explanation: The root 'kship' means to throw, cast, or propel something. It belongs to the 6th group (Tudadi Gana) and takes both Parasmaipada and Atmanepada terminations without changing its primary meaning. In the causative (Nich), it means to cause someone to throw or dispatch.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: Kartari prayoga (active voice), Parasmaipada, Lat lakara (present tense)
scenarios.example_english: The boy throws the ball.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: Kartari prayoga (active voice), Atmanepada, Lat lakara (present tense)
scenarios.example_english: The warrior discharges an arrow.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: Nich-pratyaya (causative), Lat lakara
scenarios.example_english: The father makes the boy send the letter.

vritti_extracts.madhaviya_dhatuvritti: The Madhaviya Dhatuvritti classifies 'kshipa prerane' as an Anit root belonging to the Tudadi class. It operates in both padas (Ubhayapadi) to yield 'kshipati' and 'kshipate'. The term 'prerana' denotes forceful projection or throwing (kshepana).
vritti_extracts.kshiratarangini: Kshirasvamin notes in Kshiratarangini that 'kshipa prerane' forms 'kshipati' and 'kshipate' in the present tense and 'kshepta' in the periphrastic future (Lut). The semantic emphasis is on initiating physical motion via casting, throwing, or aiming.

meanings.English: to throw, cast, propel, dispatch

dhaturupanandini.simple_explanation: The root 'chṛd' means to shine, kindle, or blaze. In the 6th group (Tudadi), it inserts a nasal sound 'n' before the final consonant in common present-tense forms, turning 'chṛd' into 'chṛndati'. When we make it causative (making something else kindle or shine), it strengthens to 'chardayati'.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: Kartari prayoga, Lat lakara (Present tense, active voice)
scenarios.example_english: The lamp shines in the darkness.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: Nic pratyaya (Causative, active voice)
scenarios.meaning: causes to kindle or illuminates something
scenarios.example_english: The boy kindles the fire.

vritti_extracts.madhaviya_dhatuvritti: The root 'chṛdī~' belongs to Tudadi-gana and carries the sense of sandipana (kindling, illuminating, or blazing brightly). Being an idit-root or belonging to the krt-group in this section, it takes the num-agama (nasal insert) yielding the base chṛnd-, producing forms like chṛndati in Sarvadhatuka environments.
vritti_extracts.kshiratarangini: Kshirasvamin notes 'chṛdī saṁdīpane' as expressing ignition and radiating glow. It participates in regular tudadi conjugational operations with num-augmentation in the present system, contrasting with standard guṇa-strengthened forms in the non-sarvadhatuka causative formations.

meanings.English: to shine, to kindle, to illuminate, to blaze

dhaturupanandini.simple_explanation: The root 'cṛt' belongs to the Tudadi class (sixth conjugation) and carries two primary senses: hurting/injuring and tying/knotting together. In the present tense, it receives an internal nasal sound ('num' augment), yielding the form 'cṛntati' (he/she knots or hurts). When converted into a causative (Nic), the vowel undergoes guna ('cartayati'), meaning 'causes to tie' or 'causes to hurt'.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: Kartari prayoga (Active Voice, Lat lakara, Prathama Purusha, Ekavacana)
scenarios.example_english: The garland maker knots the flowers together with a thread.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: Causative (Nic-pratyaya, Lat lakara, Prathama Purusha, Ekavacana)
scenarios.example_english: The teacher causes the student to tie the knot.

vritti_extracts.madhaviya_dhatuvritti: The root 'cṛtī hiṃsāgranthanayoḥ' is anudātta-it and parasmaipadi. In the sarvadhatuka environment under the Tudadi class affix 'śa', it takes the 'num' augment by the rule 'che ca' and 'śe mucādīnām', yielding 'cṛntati'. Its semantics include both physical damage (hiṃsā) and connecting or fastening elements (granthana).
vritti_extracts.kshiratarangini: Kshirasvamin notes that 'cṛtī' belongs to the kṛtādi group along with kṛt, chṛd, tṛt, and nṛt. The root takes 'num' before 'śa', forming 'cṛntati'. In ardhadhatuka contexts, intermediate optional operations (such as the optional 'it' by 'kṛtādibhyo vā' in specific tense markers) apply.

meanings.English: to hurt, injure, bind, knot, connect

dhaturupanandini.simple_explanation: The root 'kṣur' means to cut, shave, or pare. In standard active voice (Parasmaipada), it describes the direct action of cutting or shaving. When used in the causative form with the suffix 'ṇic', it signifies causing someone else to cut or get shaved.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: Tudādi class active present tense (Kartari Lat, Prathama Purusha, Ekavacana)
scenarios.example_english: The barber trims or shaves the hair.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: Causative form with ṇic affix (Hetuman Lat, Prathama Purusha, Ekavacana)
scenarios.meaning: Causes to shave or get cut
scenarios.example_english: The father has the son's hair shaved.

vritti_extracts.madhaviya_dhatuvritti: kṣura chedane. tudādirudāttaḥ parasmaibhāṣaḥ. chedanam dvidhākaranam. kṣurati, cukṣora, kṣoritā, kṣoriṣyati, akṣorīt.
vritti_extracts.kshiratarangini: kṣura chedane. kṣurati, cukṣora. kṣura iti prasiddhaṃ chedanasādhanam asmad eva nipātyate.

meanings.English: To cut, to shave, to pare
meanings.Hindi: Katna, mundana, kshura se chedan karna

dhaturupanandini.simple_explanation: The root sprs means to touch or make physical contact with something. In basic active forms (Parasmaipada), it describes an agent touching an object directly. When combined with the causative suffix nic, it shifts the meaning to causing someone or something to touch.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: kartari prayoga, laṭ lakāra, prathama puruṣa, ekavacana
scenarios.example_english: The boy touches the flower.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: ṇic pratyaya, laṭ lakāra, prathama puruṣa, ekavacana
scenarios.meaning: causes to touch / brings into contact
scenarios.example_english: The mother causes the child to touch the water.

vritti_extracts.madhaviya_dhatuvritti: The root sprs belongs to the Tudadi class and takes Parasmaipada terminations. It has the sense of samsparsana (physical touch or tactile contact). Being anit, it does not take intermediate it in non-conjugational tenses without specific exceptions, giving forms such as pasparsa in lit and asprksat or asparsit in lun.
vritti_extracts.kshiratarangini: Kshirasvamin classifies sprs under the tudadi-gana with the meaning samsparsana. It forms the present stem via the sa-vikarana (as sprsati) retaining the vocalic r in sarvadhatuka stems due to being a tudadi root.

meanings.English: to touch, to contact, to feel

dhaturupanandini.simple_explanation: The root 'tṛp' means to be satisfied, to be content, or to satisfy/gratify. In its simple present active form (Tudadi-gana), it receives an infix nasal ('num') before the suffix, producing 'tṛmpati' (he/she becomes pleased or satisfies). When used in the causative (Nic) form, it becomes 'tarpayati', meaning to gladden or offer satisfaction to someone else.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: Kartari prayoga (present active indicative, Lat lakara, prathama-purusha ekavacana)
scenarios.example_english: The boy becomes satisfied after drinking milk.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: Causative (Nic-pratyaya, Lat lakara)
scenarios.example_english: The devotee satisfies the deities with water.

vritti_extracts.madhaviya_dhatuvritti: The root 'tṛpa' belongs to Tudadi gana with the sense of 'prīṇana' (satisfaction or pleasing). By the rule 'śe mucādīnām', it takes the 'num' augment before the Sarvadhatuka affix 'śa', yielding 'tṛmpati'. In ardhadhatuka forms, guna operates according to standard sandhi rules.
vritti_extracts.kshiratarangini: Kshirasvamin explains 'tṛpa prīṇane' as signifying contentment and satiation. Belonging to the mucadi subgroup within the Tudadi class, it inserts the nasal increment in active present-system conjugation to yield 'tṛmpati'.

meanings.English: to be satisfied, to please, to gratify
meanings.Hindi: tṛpta honā, santuṣṭa honā, tṛpta karnā

dhaturupanandini.simple_explanation: The root 'ruj' primarily means 'to break', 'to fracture', or 'to cause pain'. In the Tudadi class (6th Gana), it takes the intermediate thematic affix 'ŗa' (a) without guna strengthening in the present tense, yielding 'rujati' (breaks/hurts). When used causatively with the 'nic' suffix, it becomes 'rojayati' (causes to break or causes pain).

scenarios.grammar_trigger: kartari prayoga (active voice), lat-lakara (present tense), prathama-purusha eka-vacana
scenarios.meaning: breaks, fractures, or causes pain to
scenarios.example_english: The wind breaks the tree.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: nic-pratyaya (causative), kartari prayoga, lat-lakara, prathama-purusha eka-vacana
scenarios.meaning: causes someone to break or makes something ache
scenarios.example_english: The illness causes pain in the head.

vritti_extracts.madhaviya_dhatuvritti: Madhaviya Dhatuvritti identifies 'rujā bhaṅge' in Tudadigana as an anit, parasmaipadi root. In sarvadhatuka affixes with ŗa (Tudadi), guna does not apply to the laghupadha vowel 'u' because ŗa is ṅit (viṣayatvāt), forming 'rujati'. In ardhadhatuka forms like lit, it exhibits standard guna: 'ruroja', 'rujatuḥ', 'rujuḥ'.
vritti_extracts.kshiratarangini: Kshirasvamin notes under 'rujā bhaṅge' that the root conveys physical breaking or inflicting suffering/injury (pīḍā-kartana-bhaṅgārtheṣu). The anit property prevents the augment 'iṭ' in regular ardhadhatuka formations (e.g., roktā, rokṣyati, arokṣģt).

meanings.English: to break, fracture, shatter, ache, or afflict with pain
meanings.Hindi: toḍna, bhaṅga karna, darda hona ya pida pahuncana
meanings.Bengali: bhaṅga kara, toṛaphoda kara, byatha deoya

dhaturupanandini.simple_explanation: The root 'spṛś' means to touch, feel, or come into physical contact with something. In class 6 (Tudādi), it adds the vikaraṇa '-a-' directly without guṇa strengthening of the penultimate vowel in standard present tense forms, yielding 'spṛśati'. In causative (ṇijanta) form, it means to cause to touch or sprinkle, becoming 'sparśayati'.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: Kartari prayoga (active voice), laṭ lakāra (present tense), prathama puruṣa (3rd person singular)
scenarios.example_english: The boy touches the flower with his hand.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: Causative (ṇijanta), laṭ lakāra, prathama puruṣa singular
scenarios.meaning: causes to touch / brings into contact
scenarios.example_english: The mother brings sandalwood paste into contact with the child.

vritti_extracts.madhaviya_dhatuvritti: spṛśa saṃsparśane. Tudādigaṇe aniṭ parasmaipadī. 'saṃsparśanaṃ saṃyoga-viśeṣaḥ.' Anudātteattva-lakṣaṇam aniṭ-tvaṃ spaṣṭam. Ṛkārasya guṇābhāvaḥ śasi sarvadhātukeṣu, tena spṛśati iti rūpam.
vritti_extracts.kshiratarangini: spṛśa sparśane saṃsparśe ca. Tudādiḥ aniṭ. Spraṣṭā, sparṣṭā iti ṛkārasya am-āgame rāgame ca rūpadvayam. Pasparśa, spraukṣyati/sparukṣyati.

meanings.English: to touch, perceive by touch, contact

dhaturupanandini.simple_explanation: The root ksup belongs to the 6th group of verbs (Tudadi-gana) and conveys the fundamental meaning of touching or coming into physical contact with an object. It is used in the Parasmaipada voice, taking standard active endings with the Tudadi marker (sa/a) without guna strengthening of the penultimate short vowel (forming ksupati). In causative constructions (Nic), it changes to kshopayati to mean 'causes to touch' or 'touches gently'.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: Kartari prayoga (active voice), Lat lakara (present tense), prathama-purusha, ekavacana
scenarios.example_english: The child touches the delicate flower.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: Causative (Nic-pratyaya), Kartari prayoga, Lat lakara, prathama-purusha, ekavacana
scenarios.meaning: causes to touch / brings into contact
scenarios.example_english: The mother causes the child's hand to touch.

vritti_extracts.madhaviya_dhatuvritti: The Madhaviya Dhatuvritti analyzes ksupa under the Tudadi gana with the sense of sparshana (touching or contact). Being anit and possessing a short penultimate vowel 'u' without guna in Sarvadhatuka Tudadi environments due to the Nit-like nature of Sha-pratyaya, the present third-person singular surfaces as ksupati. In Ardhadhatuka forms such as lit, it forms cukshopa.
