vritti_extracts.madhaviya_dhatuvritti: undi kledane. ikaro dighastatvat idit, tenedito nung dhatoh iti num. kledanam ardribhavanam. unatti, unttah, undanti. anit.

meanings.English: to wet, moisten, dampen

dhaturupanandini.simple_explanation: The root 'trh' belongs to the 7th class (Rudhadigana) and means 'to crush', 'to hurt', or 'to destroy'. Because it belongs to Class 7, it places a special nasal infix (na/n) right inside the root itself. When combined with strong endings like singular present tense, the special rule 'trnah im' inserts an 'i' vowel, turning the form into 'trnedhi' (he/she crushes). When made causative using the Nic suffix, it becomes 'tarhayati' (causes to crush or destroy).

vritti_extracts.kshiratarangini: Kshirasvamin defines 'trnhU himsayam' as an anit Parasmaipada root meaning destruction or injury. dhaturupanandini.simple_explanation: The root 'tṛṇ' belongs to the Tanadi class (8th Gana) and means 'to eat' or 'to graze/consume'. It adds the conjugational infix 'u' before verbal endings. In Parasmaipada, it is used when the action of eating is performed neutrally or on behalf of another, whereas in Atmanepada, it highlights that the benefit or experience of eating is directed toward the agent.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: Lat lakara, Prathama purusha, Ekavacana (Parasmaipada)
scenarios.example_english: The deer eats grass.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: Lat lakara, Prathama purusha, Ekavacana (Atmanepada)
scenarios.example_english: The animal relishes grazing on the meadow for itself.

vritti_extracts.madhaviya_dhatuvritti: The Madhaviya Dhatuvritti analyzes 'tṛṇu adane' within the Tanadi-gana, identifying the root as taking the vikaraṇa 'u' by 'tanādikṛñbhyaḥ uḥ'. It undergoes guna in sarvadhatuka contexts before vocalic/consonantal non-aprakrita endings where applicable, forming 'tṛṇoti' and 'tṛṇute'.
vritti_extracts.kshiratarangini: Kshirasvamin in Kshiratarangini explains 'tṛṇu adane' as signifying the process of consumption (bhakṣaṇārthe). It is listed among the Tanadi roots marked with anubandha 'u', confirming its Ubhayapada character and anit classification in classical derivation.

meanings.English: to eat, to graze, to consume

dhaturupanandini.simple_explanation: The root 'ghrnu' belongs to the Tanadi class (8th conjugation) and means 'to shine' or 'to glow'. In the present tense, it takes the class sign 'u', giving standard forms like 'ghrnoti' in Parasmaipada and 'ghrnute' in Atmanepada without changing its fundamental sense of illuminating or shining brightly.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: Kartari prayoga, Parasmaipada, Prathama-purusha, Ekavacana
scenarios.example_english: The sun shines with brilliance in the morning.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: Kartari prayoga, Atmanepada, Prathama-purusha, Ekavacana
scenarios.example_english: The lamp glows by itself in the darkness.

vritti_extracts.madhaviya_dhatuvritti: ghṛṇu dīptau iti tanādiḥ. u-pratyaye sarvadhatuke ghrnoti, ghrnute iti rupa-siddhiḥ. asya dhi-bhavadayo gunadikarani vidhante.
vritti_extracts.kshiratarangini: ghṛṇu dīptau. prakashanarthe vartate. tanaditvat u-vikaranaḥ. ghrnoti, ghrnute.

meanings.English: to shine, to glow, to illuminate

dhaturupanandini.simple_explanation: The root 'van' belongs to the 8th Gana (Tanadi group) and means to beg, ask, or solicit. It takes the conjugational affix 'u' (u-vikarana). Because it is an Ubhayapadi root, it can take both Parasmaipada and Atmanepada endings depending on whether the action or its benefit is general or directed toward oneself.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: Active Voice (Kartari Prayoga), Parasmaipada, Lat Lakara, Prathama Purusha, Ekavacana
scenarios.meaning: He or she asks for or begs for (something)
scenarios.example_english: The beggar asks for money.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: Active Voice (Kartari Prayoga), Atmanepada, Lat Lakara, Prathama Purusha, Ekavacana
scenarios.meaning: He or she solicits or requests (for personal benefit)
scenarios.example_english: The monk requests alms for himself.

vritti_extracts.madhaviya_dhatuvritti: The root vaṇu is listed in the Tanadi Gana under the meaning yācana (soliciting, begging). Due to the general rule for Tanadi roots, it takes the vikaraṇa 'u' (tanādikṛñbhya uḥ). By virtue of being anudāttet, it functions in both padas or specifically according to context. Its forms in present tense include vanoti and vanute.
vritti_extracts.kshiratarangini: Kshirasvamin notes vaṇu in the sense of yācana (supplication, requesting). The nasal ending behaves according to sandhi and pratyaya rules with the 'u' affix forming base stems like vano-/vanu-.

meanings.English: to beg, to ask for, to solicit

dhaturupanandini.simple_explanation: The root 'man' (manu~) in the Tanadi group means to understand, perceive, or reflect upon. Because it belongs to the 8th conjugation, it takes the intermediate affix 'u' before its verb endings and operates in Atmanepada. Adding the causative suffix changes the meaning to making someone understand, appeasing, or showing honor.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: kartari prayoga, lat-lakara, prathama-purusha, eka-vacana (Tanadi u-vikarana + Atmanepada)
scenarios.example_english: The student understands the preceptor's instruction.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: nic-pratyaya (causative), kartari prayoga, lat-lakara, prathama-purusha, eka-vacana
scenarios.meaning: causes to understand, persuades, or honors
scenarios.example_english: The mother appeases the angry child.

vritti_extracts.madhaviya_dhatuvritti: The Madhaviya Dhatuvritti identifies 'manu avabodhane' as an anudattopadesha root in Tanadi-gana, taking the 'u' vikarana per rule 'tanadikrnbhyah uh'. Being marked with an anudatta vowel as an it-marker, it exclusively takes Atmanepada affixes in non-causative active voice (yielding forms such as manute, manvate, and mene in the perfect tense).
vritti_extracts.kshiratarangini: Kshirasvamin in Kshiratarangini defines 'avabodhana' as grasping or cognitive perception (jnana). He contrasts this Tanadi-gana root (which takes the 'u' affix producing manute) with the Divadi-gana root 'mana' (which takes 'syan' yielding manyate).

meanings.English: to understand, to perceive, to think, to know

dhaturupanandini.simple_explanation: The root 'dhṛṇ' belongs to the Tanadi group (8th conjugation) and means to hurt, harm, or injure. It takes the conjugation affix 'u' (u-pratyaya) before personal endings. In Parasmaipada (dhṛṇoti), the action is directed outwards towards someone or something else. In Atmanepada (dhṛṇute), it implies an internal or reflexive engagement of the action.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: kartari prayoga (active voice), Parasmaipada, prathama-puruṣa, eka-vacana
scenarios.example_english: The hunter strikes the deer with an arrow.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: kartari prayoga (active voice), Ātmanepada, prathama-puruṣa, eka-vacana
scenarios.meaning: inflicts harm / harms oneself or for one's own sake
scenarios.example_english: The wicked person brings harm upon himself.

vritti_extracts.madhaviya_dhatuvritti: dhṛṇu hiṁsāyām - tanādibhyaḥ uḥ iti u-pratyayaḥ. sārvadhātuke guṇāvādeśa-pravṛttiḥ. ubhayato-bhāṣātvāt parasmaipadam ātmanepadaṁ ca bhavati. dhṛṇoti, dhṛṇute iti rūpadrayaṁ sidhyati.
vritti_extracts.kshiratarangini: dhṛṇu hiṁsāyām - aṇvantasya tanukaraṇa-gaṇe pāṭhaḥ. dhṛṇoti, dhṛṇute. hiṁsārthe vartamānaḥ sakarmakaḥ.

meanings.English: to hurt, to injure, to kill, to harm
meanings.Bengali: himsa kora, aghat kora, hotya kora

dhaturupanandini.simple_explanation: The root 'kr' fundamentally means 'to do', 'to make', or 'to perform'. Because it is an Ubhayapadi root, it takes Parasmaipada terminations when the action is intended generally or for someone else, and Atmanepada terminations when the fruit of the action accrues directly to the agent. When the causative suffix nic is added, it changes from doing an action to getting an action done by another person.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: Parasmaipada (Kartari Prayoga, Lat Lakara, Prathama Purusha, Ekavacana)
scenarios.meaning: He or she does / performs (for another or in general)
scenarios.example_english: The boy does the work.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: Atmanepada (Kartari Prayoga with Svaritanjit rule for self-benefit)
scenarios.meaning: He or she makes / creates (for oneself)
scenarios.example_english: The sculptor creates a statue for himself.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: Causative (Nic-pratyaya, Parasmaipada)
scenarios.meaning: Causes someone else to do or build
scenarios.example_english: The king has the temple built by the architect.

vritti_extracts.madhaviya_dhatuvritti: The root 'Dukrn' belongs to the Tanadi group having an it-marker Du at the beginning to indicate the formation of ktrima affixes (such as tri-pratyaya in ktrima) and a marker n at the end to signify Ubhayapada status via svaritn-nitah kartrabhipraye kriyaphale. It replaces its vikarana with u (tanadikrnbyah u) and undergoes regular guna or vriddhi in specified sarvadhatuka and ardhadhatuka environments.
vritti_extracts.kshiratarangini: Kshirasvamin notes that Dukrn karane stands as the comprehensive action-denoting verb among all roots, expressing general vyapara (activity). It takes the u-pratyaya in tanadigana and forms the standard paradigmatic paradigms such as karoti, kurute, cakara, cakre, karti, and karisyati, possessing universal scope across Vedic and Classical texts.

meanings.English: to do, to make, to perform, to produce, to create
meanings.Hindi: karna, banana, rachna karna, sampanna karna
meanings.Bengali: kora, banano, sampadan kora, toiri kora

dhaturupanandini.simple_explanation: The root kri means to buy or exchange goods for money. Because it has an anubandha n, it can take both Parasmaipada (krīnati) and Atmanepada (krinite) endings. When the action is done generally or for someone else, Parasmaipada is common; when the benefit is for oneself, Atmanepada is used. When prefixed with the upasarga vi-, it shifts meaning to 'to sell' (vikrīnati / vikrinite).

scenarios.grammar_trigger: Kartari prayoga, Parasmaipada, Lat-lakara, 3rd person singular with sna-vikarana
scenarios.example_english: The boy buys a book in the market.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: Upasarga vi + Kartari prayoga, Atmanepada, Lat-lakara, 3rd person singular
scenarios.example_english: The merchant sells fruit.

vritti_extracts.madhaviya_dhatuvritti: The root dukrin dravyavinimaye belongs to Kryadi gana and takes the sna vikarana by the rule kryadibhyah sna. Because of the initial du and final n markers, it is anit and ubhayapadi. In sarvadhatuka forms, sna becomes nina or ni before certain terminations.
vritti_extracts.kshiratarangini: Kshirasvamin notes krin dravyavinimaye as the head of the ninth class. He clarifies the alternation between Parasmaipada and Atmanepada driven by svaniti/pararthata and demonstrates perfect forms such as cikraya and cikriye.

meanings.English: to buy, purchase, exchange for price

dhaturupanandini.simple_explanation: The root lī means to cling, adhere, stick to, or embrace. As a Kryadi class root, it inserts the -nā- affix (śnā) before strong terminations. It is Ubhayapada, meaning it takes active (Parasmaipada) endings when expressing standard actions and middle (Atmanepada) endings when the outcome or emotional adherence relates directly to the subject.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: Parasmaipada, Kartari Prayoga (Present 3rd Person Singular)
scenarios.example_english: The creeper clings to the tree.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: Atmanepada, Kartari Prayoga (Present 3rd Person Singular)
scenarios.example_english: The child clings to the mother.

vritti_extracts.madhaviya_dhatuvritti: līñ śleṣaṇe - kryādiranidubhayapadī. śnā-pratyayaḥ. Halādi-śnā-pratyayāt pūrvam ī-kārasya hrasvatvam na bhavati, kintu 'lī-nā-ti', 'lī-nī-te' ityādi rūpāṇi sidhyanti.
vritti_extracts.kshiratarangini: līñ śleṣaṇe. śleṣaṇam āliṅganam saṁśleṣo vā. līnāti, līnīte. ni-pūrvaḥ nilīyate iti divādyantargatasya rūpam, atra tu kryādau śnāpratyaye līnāti līnīte iti jñeyam.

meanings.English: to cling, to adhere, to embrace, to melt into

dhaturupanandini.simple_explanation: The root 'pū' belongs to the Kryadi group (9th class) and means to purify, cleanse, or filter. Because it carries an anubandha 'ñ' (ñ-it), it can be conjugated in both Parasmaipada (punāti) and Atmanepada (punīte). In the present tense, it takes the class sign 'śnā' which changes to 'nā/nī' before terminations.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: Parasmaipada active voice (kartari prayoga)
scenarios.example_english: The water of the Ganga purifies everything.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: Atmanepada active voice with self-directed benefit or reflexive nuance
scenarios.example_english: The spiritual seeker purifies himself through austerity.

vritti_extracts.madhaviya_dhatuvritti: pūñ pavane - kryādi-gaṇa ubhayapada aniṭ. pavanaṃ śodhanaṃ pūtībhāvaśca. śnā-pratyaye kṛte 'halastrasya' ityādinā pratyayasya īkārādyādeśe punāti, punītaḥ, punanti, punīte ityādīni rūpāṇi bhavanti.
vritti_extracts.kshiratarangini: pūñ pavane. pavanam viśodhana-kriyā. pūnāti pūnīte vā śodhayatītyarthaḥ. ñittvād ubhayatobhāṣā.

meanings.English: to purify, to cleanse, to filter, to refine
